title: National 811 Day: Damaging Underground Utility Lines During Digging Can be a Serious Public Safety Issue
summary: Most every day, somewhere in Pacific Gas and Electric's (PGE) service area in Northern and Central California, an underground utility line is damaged due to digging. Each of these incidents pose a public safety risk requiring a 911 response and can result in repair bills averaging $3,500. To help prevent these incidents and to raise awareness of the importance of calling 811 before any digging project, large or small, Tuesday, August 11 is recognized as National 811 Day. Not contacting 811 before digging is the top driver of damages to buried utilities every year. In PGE's service area alone, there were over 1,200 line strikes during 2025, and in 55% of these incidents, 811 was not called. Underground utility lines can be shallow, sometimes only a few inches below the surface, so it is important to call 811 before any project that involves digging, even for seemingly small projects like building or replacing a fence, planting and landscaping.
